title: Anatomy of a Rubric Worksheet
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Open Educational Resources
description: Find the eight parts of a rubric worksheet on a drawing of a printed sheet, then identify each part from a description of how it looks.

learningObjectives: The learner will identify the eight parts of a rubric worksheet from a description of each part's appearance, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt.
prerequisites: The terms rubric worksheet and review checklist

dependencies: None. The drawing is inline SVG and the script is plain JavaScript.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore, then quiz on the same picture
keyQuestions: Which part of the sheet records the evidence?
Which half of the sheet holds which five metrics?
commonMisconceptions: The agent column must be filled in a manual review
The evidence column is optional when the score is obvious
The total box replaces the two subtotals
assessmentOpportunities: Which column holds where you looked, what you saw, and the rule you applied?
Which half of the sheet is worth 50 points and holds Open license?
Is the agent column filled in during a manual review?
Does the total box replace the two subtotals?

controls.name: Explore and Quiz me buttons
controls.description: switch modes. Quiz me starts a new run.

controls.name: The eight numbered markers
controls.description: hover, focus with the Tab key, or click.
